approach.method_basis: The Parent searches from one scored current molecule. It samples local atom, bond, path and ring edits, including a direct exchange of aromatic nitrogen and carbon that preserves molecular formula. It normalizes molecular identities, rejects duplicates and submits the first complete batch allowed by its short-term memory of inverse local structural changes. After receiving real scores, it moves to the highest-scoring accepted neighbor even when that move is worse than the current state. Exact score ties currently go to the lexically first canonical identity. A separate best-observed archive keeps its own score and canonical tie rule.
approach.novelty: Choose the molecule with the fewest heavy atoms when several accepted neighbors share the exact maximum score, then use the existing canonical ordering if sizes also tie. This lets the walk avoid some neutral graph growth without surrendering the best score available in that accepted batch. Earlier siblings changed edit generation or structural memory; the whole-branch deletion child exposed smaller proposals but often lost score and later regrew. This mechanism instead acts on an already scored tie set. It adds no deletion operator, chemistry filter or size preference outside exact maximum ties.

hypothesis: Resolve exact ties at the maximum accepted batch score by choosing the candidate with the fewest heavy atoms, then the lexicographically smallest canonical identity, while leaving every non-tied accepted maximum and the independent best archive unchanged.

finding_summary.headline: Six compact tie choices preserved immediate scores, but the panel mean fell
finding_summary.insights: Equal immediate scores do not make tied molecules equivalent starting points for the remaining search. The rule reached smaller real states and preserved the independent archive, so the missing score benefit cannot be explained by a tie implementation failure or an immediate sacrifice in accepted score. The two affected walks ended smaller than their parents yet found lower best scores, narrowing the claim: this size preference controls some neutral growth, but has not identified better future neighborhoods. The chemistry assessment reinforces the distinction between atom count and useful simplification: deco_hop proposals had slightly fewer atoms on average but greater molecular mass and more nitrogen-halogen bonds, while unusual sulfur chemistry persisted. A compact winner can also be a bond change or element substitution. Local chemical organization or neighborhood quality therefore remains a more informative open question than size alone. Six interventions in two overlapping walks do not isolate the contribution of each choice, and the sparse activation does not establish how the rule would behave on other tasks.
finding_summary.results: Six of 28 exact maximum-score ties selected a different molecule, all on deco_hop plateaus in two seeds. Every changed choice preserved the accepted maximum score and used one or two fewer heavy atoms than the lexical winner, saving ten atoms across those decisions. Three choices kept the source size and three reduced it by one atom. All 407 unique maxima retained the same choice on the same accepted batch, and the identity, archive and transition audits passed. Descendants exceeded the compact selected size after five of the six changes; the remaining case finished at that size after five further steps. Later archive improvements occurred, but the complete three-seed macro mean fell from 0.521759 to 0.520655, a paired loss of 0.001104 against the required gain of 0.002. Both affected seeds declined; all four other tasks and the third seed retained exactly the parent's molecule/score sequences.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich, often aromatic molecules with recurrent unusual sulfur, reactive halogen bonds and unresolved stereochemistry.
molecular.overall_character: Node n-770a3cefca6a covers every task in the supplied digest; tasks_without_trajectories is empty. The digest contains 900 evaluated molecules and 870 optimizer proposals per task. Its proposal ring_closure_rate is 1.0 throughout; aromatic_atom_rate ranges from 0.7184 to 1.0 and describes the presence of aromatic SMILES tokens, not the fraction of atoms that are aromatic. These are substantial heterocyclic and polycyclic graphs, not small acyclic fragments. Passive RDKit 2023.09.6 parsing of all 4350 proposals succeeds: they contain 21-49 heavy atoms, with median 33, and 2-10 perceived rings, with median 4. Graph parsing does not establish energetic stability or a synthesis. Relatively conventional indole carboxamides coexist with heavily decorated nitrogen heterocycles, sulfur-rich cages, medium-ring bridges, heteroatom-halogen bonds and unusual neutral sulfur multiple bonding. Some individual structures are plausible, but repeated problematic chemistry among the reported high scorers and late proposals supports the overall implausible/weak reading. Diversity is moderate at the graph level across the panel; high scorers within a task frequently remain closely related members of a local family. All proposal charged_rate and stereocentre_rate counters are 0.0. This means no explicit charge or stereochemical labels, not an absence of ionizable atoms or stereogenic graphs: 3432 proposals have potential unassigned stereocentres in the passive audit. Against Parent n-abcd951ab7cc, all molecule/score sequences match exactly on four tasks; only deco_hop seeds 0 and 2 differ. The chemistry comparison below concerns those observed outputs and makes no activation finding. All descriptor counts and parent comparisons are reproducible in .slots/SPIRAL2.r0012-03-improve-L16.molecular-audit.json; they describe proposal occurrences, and perceived ring counts can include overlapping rings in bridged systems. The digest final_molecules are the last proposal records from seed 2, not a selected endpoint or the best archive.

method_name: Tabu search: de novo graph walks with expiring structural prohibitions
method_thesis: The anchor is the basic tabu-search procedure in Section 2 of [Glover, Tabu Search—Part I](https://leeds-faculty.colorado.edu/glover/TS%20-%20Part%20I-ORSA-aw.pdf), fixed before locating this external source. It chooses the best available admissible move, including a worsening move, while temporarily prohibiting reversals through short-term attribute memory. My molecular adaptation starts from the best supplied observation and maintains one current molecular graph, its true score, an independent best-observed archive, and expiring structural restrictions. At each feedback step, stochastically generate a new neighborhood through atom and bond edits, additions, deletions and chemically checked ring changes. Define move attributes from presence/absence changes of canonical local subgraphs around the edited region. After selecting a move, temporarily forbid a bounded record of its inverse attribute changes. These restrictions must apply to different canonical molecules sharing the affected local chemistry, so they can alter search beyond the protocol's mandatory whole-molecule duplicate rejection. Generate valid, canonical-unique, admissible neighbors until the announced batch is filled, then submit them directly without a learned score predictor. Only after real feedback choose the highest-scoring accepted neighbor as the next current graph, even when it scores below the current graph; retain the best score seen anywhere. Age restrictions by completed walk steps. If restrictions prevent sufficient fresh generation, release the oldest restrictions only as needed and record that release. This root uses the basic tabu form without an aspiration rule requiring unknown candidate scores. Preparation needs no learned model or corpus molecule store. Each objective restarts the same task-agnostic procedure with clean labeled and tabu state, and every proposed structure is generated online from the evolving current graph. The hypothesis is that an aggressive observed-neighbor choice combined with temporary structural reversal restrictions can move through useful intermediate structures and reach higher scoring molecular regions within the supplied feedback schedule. Activation requires restrictions to veto otherwise valid novel structural moves and thereby influence later current states. That diagnostic is insufficient by itself: success is the mean of the five independent final Top-1 scores. Overbroad attributes may suppress productive chemistry, while overly specific attributes may never affect novel proposals; the root must expose both possibilities.

finding_summary.headline: Six compact tie choices preserved immediate scores, but the panel mean fell
finding_summary.insights: Equal immediate scores do not make tied molecules equivalent starting points for the remaining search. The rule reached smaller real states and preserved the independent archive, so the missing score benefit cannot be explained by a tie implementation failure or an immediate sacrifice in accepted score. The two affected walks ended smaller than their parents yet found lower best scores, narrowing the claim: this size preference controls some neutral growth, but has not identified better future neighborhoods. The chemistry assessment reinforces the distinction between atom count and useful simplification: deco_hop proposals had slightly fewer atoms on average but greater molecular mass and more nitrogen-halogen bonds, while unusual sulfur chemistry persisted. A compact winner can also be a bond change or element substitution. Local chemical organization or neighborhood quality therefore remains a more informative open question than size alone. Six interventions in two overlapping walks do not isolate the contribution of each choice, and the sparse activation does not establish how the rule would behave on other tasks.
finding_summary.results: Six of 28 exact maximum-score ties selected a different molecule, all on deco_hop plateaus in two seeds. Every changed choice preserved the accepted maximum score and used one or two fewer heavy atoms than the lexical winner, saving ten atoms across those decisions. Three choices kept the source size and three reduced it by one atom. All 407 unique maxima retained the same choice on the same accepted batch, and the identity, archive and transition audits passed. Descendants exceeded the compact selected size after five of the six changes; the remaining case finished at that size after five further steps. Later archive improvements occurred, but the complete three-seed macro mean fell from 0.521759 to 0.520655, a paired loss of 0.001104 against the required gain of 0.002. Both affected seeds declined; all four other tasks and the third seed retained exactly the parent's molecule/score sequences.

molecular_assessment.headline: Ring-rich, often aromatic molecules with recurrent unusual sulfur, reactive halogen bonds and unresolved stereochemistry.
molecular_assessment.overall_character: Node n-770a3cefca6a covers every task in the supplied digest; tasks_without_trajectories is empty. The digest contains 900 evaluated molecules and 870 optimizer proposals per task. Its proposal ring_closure_rate is 1.0 throughout; aromatic_atom_rate ranges from 0.7184 to 1.0 and describes the presence of aromatic SMILES tokens, not the fraction of atoms that are aromatic. These are substantial heterocyclic and polycyclic graphs, not small acyclic fragments. Passive RDKit 2023.09.6 parsing of all 4350 proposals succeeds: they contain 21-49 heavy atoms, with median 33, and 2-10 perceived rings, with median 4. Graph parsing does not establish energetic stability or a synthesis. Relatively conventional indole carboxamides coexist with heavily decorated nitrogen heterocycles, sulfur-rich cages, medium-ring bridges, heteroatom-halogen bonds and unusual neutral sulfur multiple bonding. Some individual structures are plausible, but repeated problematic chemistry among the reported high scorers and late proposals supports the overall implausible/weak reading. Diversity is moderate at the graph level across the panel; high scorers within a task frequently remain closely related members of a local family. All proposal charged_rate and stereocentre_rate counters are 0.0. This means no explicit charge or stereochemical labels, not an absence of ionizable atoms or stereogenic graphs: 3432 proposals have potential unassigned stereocentres in the passive audit. Against Parent n-abcd951ab7cc, all molecule/score sequences match exactly on four tasks; only deco_hop seeds 0 and 2 differ. The chemistry comparison below concerns those observed outputs and makes no activation finding. All descriptor counts and parent comparisons are reproducible in .slots/SPIRAL2.r0012-03-improve-L16.molecular-audit.json; they describe proposal occurrences, and perceived ring counts can include overlapping rings in bridged systems. The digest final_molecules are the last proposal records from seed 2, not a selected endpoint or the best archive.

applicability_conditions: The rule applies only after real finite scores have joined the current batch proposals, and only to exact accepted maxima. It never trades a measured score difference for compactness, treats a near tie as equal, or selects from the independent archive.

The Parent provides sparse actual opportunities: only three of its 435 completed batches would change under this criterion, all on source-score plateaus in one task. Changed trajectories may expose different opportunities, but broad activation across tasks is not assumed and no quota or threshold adjustment will force it.

Heavy-atom count is a deterministic task-agnostic descriptor of the accepted graph. It is a size preference only; smaller graphs can have less favorable future neighborhoods, reactive chemistry, strained rings or poorer eventual scores.

The inherited aromatic nitrogen relocation, repaired canonical identities and short-term inverse-motif memory are retained. A different tied winner may have different motif changes and therefore install different restrictions through the unchanged selected-transition event.

The Knowledge-only whole-branch deletion cluster concerns expanded proposal generation with multi-atom pruning. Its losses and regrowth motivate score-preserving tie selection, but it did not test this accepted-transition mechanism. No supplied sibling or Curate cluster has tested minimum-heavy-atom resolution of exact accepted-score maxima; this is a distinct mechanism, not a retry of that deletion menu.

Only supplied local feedback and already accepted molecular graphs enter the algorithm. The full panel, announced batch, budgets, seeds and timeouts remain protocol-owned; passive saved-batch comparisons are selection diagnostics rather than new oracle evaluations or alternative complete walks.

approach.method_basis: The Parent searches from one scored current molecule. It samples local atom, bond, path and ring edits, including a direct exchange of aromatic nitrogen and carbon that preserves molecular formula. It normalizes molecular identities, rejects duplicates and submits the first complete batch allowed by its short-term memory of inverse local structural changes. After receiving real scores, it moves to the highest-scoring accepted neighbor even when that move is worse than the current state. Exact score ties currently go to the lexically first canonical identity. A separate best-observed archive keeps its own score and canonical tie rule.
approach.novelty: Choose the molecule with the fewest heavy atoms when several accepted neighbors share the exact maximum score, then use the existing canonical ordering if sizes also tie. This lets the walk avoid some neutral graph growth without surrendering the best score available in that accepted batch. Earlier siblings changed edit generation or structural memory; the whole-branch deletion child exposed smaller proposals but often lost score and later regrew. This mechanism instead acts on an already scored tie set. It adds no deletion operator, chemistry filter or size preference outside exact maximum ties.
